_readme: THE ASSET LICENCE REGISTER — [pipeline K-10]/[K-11] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/08-compliance-legal.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
One row for every asset that ships inside a build, with the licence it ships under and the SOURCE of
that licence claim. Plus the other half of K-11: every app shows those licences from a real screen.
WHY IT EXISTS. Both major stores can ask for evidence of rights to material an app ships, and a
review can be held or a listing pulled while the evidence is produced. That demand arrives without
warning and is answered in hours or not at all. Before this file the answer would have been a search
through a build directory; now it is a file.
🔴 EVERY ROW CARRIES A SOURCE FOR ITS LICENCE CLAIM, AND THE GUARD REFUSES A ROW WITHOUT ONE.
This is the same rule tooling/channel-register.json enforces for numeric limits: a field whose value
was not fetched from a primary source is recorded as UNVERIFIED and is NOT given a plausible one. An
invented licence looks exactly like a researched one and is worth nothing in the one conversation it
exists for.
🔴 AND THE HEADLINE EXAMPLE IS IN THIS FILE. ~~The stage document states twice that Flutter's bundled
MaterialIcons font is CC-BY 4.0. Google's material-design-icons repository has published under
Apache-2.0 since 2016; CC-BY 4.0 was the project's EARLIER licence. Neither could be confirmed from a
primary source in this environment, so the row below says UNVERIFIED and names the file that would
settle it.~~ SETTLED 2026-08-13 — AND BOTH SIDES WERE RIGHT ABOUT DIFFERENT ARTEFACTS, which is why
the disagreement was stable enough to survive in the corpus: google/material-design-icons @ master is
Apache-2.0; the font Flutter VENDORS is CC BY 4.0, per materialicons_license.txt:1 in the artifact that
bin/internal/material_fonts.version pins. The tie-breaker is the file that SHIPS. THE GUARD DESIGN
SURVIVED EITHER ANSWER — 'fail on any shipped asset with no row' is licence-agnostic — which is why
guessing would have bought nothing and cost the register its credibility.
⚠️ AND THE ANSWER AROSE A DUTY THE ROW HAD RECORDED AS `null`. CC BY 4.0 §3(a)(1) requires attribution
on Sharing, and the shipped bundle carries none of it: 0 occurrences of 'Attribution 4.0 International',
'CC BY' or 'material-design-icons' across 33,785 lines of apps/subscriptiontracker/build/web/assets/NOTICES. So the
verified answer turned a quiet UNVERIFIED row into an open, build-failing breach — see the row's
`attributionGap`. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is not 'UNVERIFIED is bad' (it was the honest call then):
AN UNREAD LICENCE IMPLIES AN UNKNOWN DUTY, so `attributionRequired` must never be left at `null` beside
one. Two compounding unknowns render as a confident blank, and a blank is what nobody re-opens.
TWO ENUMERATION MODES, and the difference is deliberate:
· DECLARED (default) — every file under a `flutter: assets:` entry in every workspace pubspec,
every declared font file, and the icon font implied by `uses-material-design: true`. Runs in the
guards lane on every push, with no Flutter toolchain needed.
· BUNDLE (`--bundle <dir>`) — walks a real built bundle. Runs in the app_brick lane after
`flutter build web`, which is where the DECLARED set and the SHIPPED set can be seen to differ.
⚠️ The declared mode is the weaker of the two and says so: it reads intent, not output. It is the
mode that runs everywhere, and the bundle mode is the one that can catch a build that ships something
nobody declared.
⚠️ LICENCES THAT ARE ARCHITECTURALLY INCOMPATIBLE ARE REFUSED, not merely noted. CC-BY-NC forbids
commercial use — that one is unchanged and needs no argument, since commercial distribution is the
entire business.
🔴 THE SHAREALIKE BAN WAS RE-BASED 2026-08-13. IT WAS RIGHT, FOR A REASON THAT COULD NOT BE RIGHT.
~~CC-BY-SA forbids Effective Technological Measures; our content packs are Ed25519-signed with a
fail-closed verifier (packages/core/lib/src/content/pack_verifier.dart), which is exactly such a
measure.~~ RETRACTED: that clause does not distinguish SA from BY. The anti-ETM term is §2(a)(5)(b)
'No downstream restrictions', and it is VERBATIM IN PLAIN CC BY 4.0 — read it at
bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts/materialicons_license.txt:175-180 in the very font this register
now clears under CC BY. A reason that convicts SA convicts the icon font in every app we ship, so it
proved too much: either the reason was wrong or our own bundle was contraband. The reason was wrong.
(The signature question itself is untouched and still open on its own merits — an Ed25519 signature
over a pack is an integrity check, and whether it 'restricts exercise of the Licensed Rights by a
recipient' is a real question. It is simply not the question that separates these two licences.)
THE HONEST GROUND IS §3(b) COPYLEFT-ON-MODIFICATION, and it is decisive here because of what this
factory DOES to what it ships. CC BY 4.0's Section 3 contains exactly one subsection — 'a.
Attribution' (materialicons_license.txt:215, and Section 4 begins at :262 with nothing between). CC
BY-SA adds a §3(b) ShareAlike, whose obligations attach to ADAPTED MATERIAL: share an adaptation and
the Adapter's Licence must itself be BY-SA. We subset fonts and recolour images, so what we ship is
adapted as a matter of routine — MEASURED, not assumed: Flutter's icon tree-shaking rewrites
MaterialIcons from 1,645,184 bytes to 11,524 in apps/subscriptiontracker/build/web/assets/fonts/, a new OTTO file
rather than a copy. Under SA that would force a copyleft licence onto the shipped artefact, which is
incompatible with a proprietary all-rights-reserved binary. THAT is why SA cannot ship here.
⚠️ AND THE BAN IS DELIBERATELY NOT OVER-CLAIMED, because an over-broad rule gets waived and then
ignored. BUNDLING ALONE IS A COLLECTION, NOT AN ADAPTATION: merely placing an unmodified SA asset
beside our own files in a bundle does not produce Adapted Material and would not trigger §3(b). The
prefix ban is therefore stricter than the licence strictly requires, and that is a deliberate,
recorded choice — this factory has no route that ships a third-party asset WITHOUT transforming it,
so a per-asset 'was this one adapted?' exception would be a question nobody can answer at review time.
If such a route is ever built, this is the paragraph to re-open. An asset under either prefix cannot
ship here at all, so the guard fails rather than printing.
🔴 EVERY ROW ANSWERS THE SEAM QUESTION — `contentFamily` + `contentFamilyWhy`, REQUIRED (2026-08-13).
This file and content-licence-register.json are DIFFERENT QUESTIONS (that file's own _readme draws the
boundary, and [7]P-5 and [8]K-10 now both quote it verbatim in their requirement texts):
this file                     — what a BUILT APP BUNDLE ships
content-licence-register.json — what the CONTENT PIPELINE consumes to PRODUCE a pack
An app can ship a font it never generated with; a pack can carry a voice the app binary never sees.
A family can legitimately be in BOTH, and until 2026-08-13 nothing compared what the two files said about
one — two green guards, one family, two possible licence verdicts, and the disagreement invisible because
each guard was doing its own job correctly. So every row here names the content family it corresponds to,
or `null` for 'the content pipeline does not consume this', plus one sentence saying why. The field is
REQUIRED and `null` is a real answer: an OPTIONAL cross-link cannot fail on the input that actually causes
a seam, which is nobody writing the link. Where a row names a family, tooling/ci/licence-cross-assert.mjs
fails the build unless both registers record the SAME licence identity and the SAME attribution duty —
and it is imported by BOTH guards, so a disagreement turns both red rather than leaving one quotable.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-licence-register.mjs. See tooling/legal/README.md for the public/private
split — nothing here is private: a licence claim with no public source is not a licence claim.
🔴 `appScopedAssets` (2026-09-26, lead ruling PRL-R1): WHAT ONE APP SHIPS BECAUSE ONE OF ITS PACKAGES DOES.
A pub package an app depends on puts its own assets into that app's bundle under packages/<pkg>/, and no
workspace manifest declares them, so the `assets` rows above (the workspace's own material and the
toolchain's) cannot say 'this app ships that file'. Each app-scoped row names its scope `app:<app_id>`, the
path inside that app's built assets directory, the PACKAGE that ships it (a pub package, or `sdk:flutter`
for an engine or web asset of the SDK) and the licence id. The licence is not taken on trust: the
`--bundle <dir> --app <id>` walk reads the package's own LICENSE through the app's resolved
package_config.json and fails when the two differ, and it fails with COVERAGE LOST when no `pub get` ran.
That walk resolves every file in the bundle to exactly one row — a row above, or one scoped to THIS app —
so an `app:<other>` row never satisfies an app, and a new app's rows come from its own bundle. The rows
live in their own array so that every row above keeps its shape, and a guard that predates the array
reads this file exactly as it did.

_why: Floors measured on the tree the day this file landed: 12 pubspec.yaml files, 3 declared asset files
(apps/subscriptiontracker/assets/brand/). A walk that finds fewer has BROKEN — an assets: entry renamed, a
directory moved — and an asset register that enumerates nothing reports every asset accounted for.
🔴 minDeclaredAssets WAS 3 AND IS NOW 2, LOWERED DELIBERATELY ON 2026-08-17. It was NOT lowered to
make a red guard go green: apps/subscriptiontracker/assets/brand/ genuinely holds two files now, because
nikatru-icon.png was deleted as an exact duplicate — sha256 e1b05e51aee8617b02721b04c30e2bb898e327de
52082675dc7eba200cfb41fc, byte-for-byte and 261,948 bytes identical to the launcher master at
apps/subscriptiontracker/assets/icon/app_icon_1024.png, which is NOT under a declared assets: entry and so never
shipped. The duplicate sat in the one directory that does ship, putting 256 KB of it into all six
platform bundles with no Dart string naming it. Zero unique bytes left the repo; its row
(`brand-nikatru-icon`) went in the same change, and the reason text it carried was promoted onto
brand-nikatru-logo rather than dropped, so the two surviving rows cite a live id.
⚠️ THE FLOOR MOVES ONLY WITH A DELETION THAT IS WRITTEN DOWN, AND IT IS NEVER REMOVED. Lowering a
REQUIRED_COVERAGE number to match whatever the walk happened to find is precisely how a guard stops
checking while still printing ok. Negative-tested on the real tree the day it moved: deleting a
second brand PNG dropped the walk to 1 and assert-licence-register.mjs exited 1 on this floor.
🔴 FILES THE BUILD ITSELF EMITS INTO THE BUNDLE, WHICH ARE NOT MATERIAL WE SHIPPED FROM ANYWHERE.
Every one is named individually and given a reason. This is NOT a pattern and NOT a suffix rule: a
NEW filename appearing in a real bundle still FAILS until somebody writes it down, which is the
whole value. An `*.json`-shaped exclusion would have swallowed a third-party data file the day one
arrived.
They were found the honest way. The DECLARED-mode walk reads pubspec manifests and could never see
any of them; the first run of the --bundle mode against a real `flutter build web` output failed
naming six files. That is the two modes doing exactly what they exist to do — intent and output
differ, and the difference is only visible against a build.

files.AssetManifest.bin: the build's own index of which assets it packaged, in binary form. Generated from the pubspecs at build time; it describes assets rather than being one.
files.AssetManifest.bin.json: the same index, JSON-wrapped for the web loader.
files.AssetManifest.json: the legacy JSON form of the same index, still emitted by some toolchain versions.
files.FontManifest.json: the build's index of which font families it packaged. Generated, and it describes fonts rather than containing one.
files.NOTICES: 🔴 THE ATTRIBUTION SURFACE ITSELF, not an asset needing one. Flutter concatenates the licence texts of everything linked into the build and ships them here; the framework's LicensePage reads it. It is what an `attributionRequired` row would POINT AT, so requiring it to carry its own licence row would be circular.

_why: Refused outright rather than flagged. Both prefixes below are incompatible with how this factory
SHIPS, not merely inconvenient: CC-BY-NC excludes commercial distribution, which is the entire
business; ~~CC-BY-SA's anti-ETM term is refuted by the Ed25519 pack signature we cannot remove
without removing the fail-closed verifier that makes shipped content trustworthy.~~ RE-BASED
2026-08-13 — the anti-ETM term is §2(a)(5)(b) and is verbatim in plain CC BY 4.0 too, so it could
never separate SA from BY; it would have condemned the CC BY icon font this register clears. The
operative ground is §3(b) copyleft-on-modification: SA's obligations attach to ADAPTED Material, and
this factory subsets fonts (measured: 1,645,184 → 11,524 bytes) and recolours images, so it adapts
almost everything it ships. Bundling alone would be a mere collection and would NOT trigger §3(b) —
the prefix ban is knowingly stricter than that, for the reason set out in _readme. Full argument and
the retraction it replaces are in this file's _readme; keep the two in step if either changes.
Matched by PREFIX so version suffixes (…-4.0, …-3.0) are covered without listing them.
🔴 RESOLVED AS A CALL SITE, NEVER AS A GREP FOR A STRING. [3]S-2 already proved in this repository
that a declaration is not a call: a constant referenced from an unrouted widget satisfies
'references it from a reachable screen' while being unreachable. Each pattern below is a
CONSTRUCTOR or FUNCTION INVOCATION — `AboutListTile(`, `showLicensePage(`,
`LicenseRegistry.addLicense(` — so a comment mentioning licences, or an import of the page that
nothing builds, does not satisfy it. Comments are stripped before matching.
⚠️ HONEST LIMIT, STATED HERE RATHER THAN IMPLIED AWAY: this proves the widget is CONSTRUCTED
somewhere in the app's lib/, not that a user can reach it in three taps. Proving reachability needs
a widget test that pumps the screen and taps the tile — that is [8]INC-5, and it lives in files
this change deliberately does not touch.

assets.contentFamilyWhy: An icon font the Flutter toolchain bundles into the binary. The content pipeline neither generates with it nor ships it inside a pack, so it is a K-10 artefact only.
assets.name: MaterialIcons (the icon font Flutter bundles under uses-material-design: true)

source.note: SETTLED 2026-08-13 BY READING THE FILE THAT SHIPS, which is the only artefact whose licence binds us. bin/internal/material_fonts.version pins the fonts archive to the hash in the URL above; it expands to bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts/, and materialicons_license.txt:1 there reads 'Attribution 4.0 International' verbatim. Canonical text: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode. 🔴 BOTH EARLIER POSITIONS WERE TRUE OF DIFFERENT ARTEFACTS, which is why the corpus could hold them at once without either side being careless: google/material-design-icons @ master is Apache-2.0, and the font Flutter actually vendors carries CC BY 4.0. The tie-breaker is not which repository is upstream but which bytes are in the bundle.

assets.wouldNeed: ~~The LICENSE file in Google's material-design-icons repository, at the revision Flutter vendors, read directly. Also open: whether a release build ships the whole font or a tree-shaken subset — a subset and a whole font are different artefacts with the same filename (see the flutter-icon-tree-shaking-scope row in tooling/legal/duty-matrix.json).~~ RESOLVED 2026-08-13, and the answer to the second half changed the first. (a) LICENCE: read from the VENDORED file, not the repository — see source.note; the repository would have given the wrong answer. (b) SUBSET: it is a subset, measured — apps/subscriptiontracker/build/web/assets/fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf is 11,524 bytes against the vendored 1,645,184, i.e. 0.7%, and its header is a freshly written `OTTO` (CFF) table. So what ships is not a copy of the licensed file but a transformation of it.
assets.shippedIn: every build of every app: apps/subscriptiontracker/pubspec.yaml and the brick's app pubspec both declare uses-material-design: true, so this font is in 100% of what we publish. Confirmed in a real bundle: apps/subscriptiontracker/build/web/assets/FontManifest.json declares family MaterialIcons → fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf.

attributionGap.duty: CC BY 4.0 §3(a)(1) (materialicons_license.txt:217-244). On Sharing we must retain, if supplied: (A)(i) identification of the creator, (ii) a copyright notice, (iii) a notice referring to this Public License, (iv) a notice referring to the disclaimer of warranties, (v) a URI to the Licensed Material; and (B) indicate if we modified it. Flutter supplies all of this beside the font, so 'if it is supplied by the Licensor' is satisfied and the retention duty is live rather than excused.
attributionGap.alsoModified: 🔴 §3(a)(1)(B) BITES TOO, AND IS THE HALF NOBODY WAS LOOKING AT. Icon tree-shaking rewrites the font (1,645,184 → 11,524 bytes), which is 'altered … or otherwise modified' under §1(a) Adapted Material. We therefore owe an indication of modification on top of the five retentions.
attributionGap.gap: 🔴 NOT DISCHARGED ANYWHERE, MEASURED IN THE SHIPPED BUNDLE 2026-08-13. apps/subscriptiontracker/build/web/assets/NOTICES is 33,785 lines and contains: 'Attribution 4.0 International' → 0 · 'CC BY' → 0 · 'material-design-icons' → 0 · 'materialicons' → 0 · 'Material Icons' → 0. Its single creativecommons.org hit (NOTICES:6501) is a CC0 zero-waive for the unrelated W3C Ahem test font. The licence text exists nowhere in this repository either.
attributionGap.whyItIsMissing: MECHANISM, not an oversight in one app: Flutter's NOTICES is assembled from the LICENSE files of Dart PACKAGES, and this font arrives from the SDK artifact cache instead. The control case is in the same file — cupertino_icons is a pub package and its licence IS present (1 hit), while Roboto, which also comes from material_fonts/, is likewise absent (0 hits). So every app built by this factory inherits the same gap, and no per-app fix generalises.
attributionGap.surfaceIsNotTheProblem: The licences SCREEN is wired and reachable: apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:690 calls showLicensePage( and :711 constructs AboutListTile(. The screen renders what LicenseRegistry holds, and what it holds does not include this licence. This is a CONTENT gap on a working surface, which is why the licenceSurfaceCalls limb is green and correct while the duty is still unmet.
attributionGap.wouldDischarge: Register the vendored text at runtime so it reaches the screen the app already has: LicenseRegistry.addLicense(() async* { yield LicenseEntryWithLineBreaks(['MaterialIcons'], <text of materialicons_license.txt>); }) in the shared chassis, carrying the creator, the copyright notice, the reference to CC BY 4.0 and its warranty disclaimer, the URI, and a line stating the font is a tree-shaken subset (§3(a)(1)(B)). Chassis, not app: the mechanism above makes this every app's gap. Doing so lets `attributedIn` name a real file and turns this row green honestly.
attributionGap.whyAttributedInIsNull: ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-13 — IT IS NO LONGER NULL, AND IT WAS NOT RESOLVED BY RENAMING THE PROBLEM. It stayed null while nothing in the tree discharged the duty, because every candidate value then available would have been a false citation: the bundle NOTICES does not contain the text AND is a gitignored build artefact (apps/subscriptiontracker/.gitignore:33 '/build/'), so it is absent from a fresh CI checkout; the vendored licence file lives in the Flutter SDK cache, outside repoRoot. The duty is now actually discharged: packages/design_system/lib/src/licences/vendored_asset_licences.dart registers the notice via LicenseRegistry.addLicense, carrying all five §3(a)(1)(A) retentions plus the §3(a)(1)(B) modification statement, with §3(a)(2)'s URI to the legalcode. apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/main.dart calls it before runApp, so it reaches the LicensePage that settings_screen.dart already offers. It is in the CHASSIS, not the app, because the mechanism made this every stamped app's gap. ⚠️ The guard checks the path EXISTS, not that the call is wired — the test that proves the entry actually reaches LicenseRegistry lives in packages/design_system/test/vendored_asset_licences_test.dart, and without it this row would be a citation to a file that could be emptied tomorrow.

assets.note: 🔴 THIS ROW WAS THE REGISTER'S OWN HEADLINE EXAMPLE OF AN HONEST UNVERIFIED, AND IT WAS ALSO HIDING A LIVE BREACH. Until 2026-08-13 it read licence UNVERIFIED with attributionRequired null. `null` there does not mean 'no duty' — it means nobody decided — but on a page of `false`s it reads as 'probably nothing owed', which is how a shipped, unattributed CC BY asset sat in plain sight in the file built to catch exactly that. The lesson is narrower than 'UNVERIFIED is bad', because UNVERIFIED was the right call at the time: it is that AN UNKNOWN LICENCE IMPLIES AN UNKNOWN DUTY, and the duty field must not be allowed to rest at `null` while the licence is unread — the two unknowns compound into a confident-looking blank.

assets.contentFamilyWhy: A text font the Flutter toolchain emits into a web bundle. The content pipeline neither generates with it nor ships it inside a pack, so it is a K-10 artefact only.
assets.name: Roboto (the text font the Flutter SDK vendors beside the icon font)

source.note: READ FROM THE BYTES THAT SHIP, the same discipline as the flutter-material-icons row above and the same artifact: bin/internal/material_fonts.version pins the archive at the hash in the URL, it expands to bin/cache/artifacts/material_fonts/, and `roboto_license.txt` there opens 'Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004' verbatim (measured 2026-09-12 in the SDK cache on the build box). 🔴 TWO FONTS, ONE ARCHIVE, TWO LICENCES: `materialicons_license.txt` beside it reads 'Attribution 4.0 International'. A single row covering 'the vendored fonts' would have attributed one of them wrongly, which is why they are separate rows with separate notices.

assets.shippedIn: MEASURED 2026-09-12, and the trigger is narrower than 'Flutter ships Roboto'. It ships in a STAMPED app's web bundle: CI's app-brick job built apps/probe on Flutter 3.47.2 with `--no-web-resources-cdn` — the flag deploy-web.yml has carried since #676 — and assert-licence-register.mjs --bundle found `Roboto-Regular.ttf` in apps/probe/build/web/assets, which is how this row came to exist. ⚠️ IT IS NOT IN THE LIVE APP: the same SDK and the same flag deployed apps/subscriptiontracker on the same day and its served bundle carries no Roboto — probed at nikatru.com/subscriptiontracker/assets/, where fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf answers font/otf 11,768 B while every Roboto path answers the SPA shell (the apex router's 200-HTML for an unknown path). A local build of the app on Flutter 3.44.9 likewise emitted none.
assets.wouldNeed: TWO measurements this row does not claim to have made, neither of which blocks the licence claim above. (a) WHY the stamped app's bundle carries it and the shipped app's does not — same SDK, same flag, same day. The next bundle walk should print the file list rather than only the offender. (b) Whether the emitted bytes are the vendored file byte-for-byte: if a build ever re-writes the font, Apache-2.0 §4(b) adds a change-notice duty on top of §4(a) and §4(c). The notice registered in the chassis states only what this application does (nothing), which is true either way.
assets.note: 🔴 THIS ROW IS THE PREDICTION IN packages/design_system/lib/src/licences/vendored_asset_licences.dart COMING TRUE UNPROMPTED. That file said Roboto was not registered because no Roboto bytes were distributed, and that 'if a future build ever ships Roboto, this file is where its entry belongs — and the asset register's row is what should catch it'. The bundle walk caught it, in CI, on the first build that emitted it — before any stamped app was deployed. The notice was then added where that comment said it belonged, and packages/design_system/test/vendored_asset_licences_test.dart proves it reaches LicenseRegistry rather than merely existing on disk.
